A month ago I spoke at RDSW (Raleigh-Durham Startup Co.) to an amazing audience of PMs, founders, and designers, all trying to figure out how AI fits into their work. The session itself was fun, but the conversations after were what stayed with me.

Since then I've been talking to customers at Airtable working through the same questions from a different angle. Their leadership is asking them to use AI more, faster, and everywhere, and they're trying to make sense of what that actually means day-to-day.

What I keep hearing in both rooms is the same thing. We're heading into uncharted territory, and most of us have a quiet voice in the back of our heads wondering if it's messier than the hype suggests, asking whether the thing everyone calls an agent really is one, and not quite sure if it's okay to say any of this out loud.

Those quiet voices are why I'm building Agent Literacy, a living, breathing knowledge hub for working through these questions out loud and in public. It's my little corner of the internet that is under construction and probably always will be.

If you've been working with AI in any role and have your own quiet voice you'd like to share, I'd love to hear it.

Check it out here → https://lnkd.in/edwXHUrF

Over the past several weeks we have launched:
‣ Timeline nesting: nest records inside other records in Timeline view, up to 7 levels deep
‣ Reschedule dependent records: when a date moves, only the work after it shifts. What you've already finished stays where it is
‣ Default dependency type & buffer: set them once for a table instead of configuring every link by hand
‣ Date dependencies in record templates: templates now carry their dependency types and buffers, so a new project starts fully wired
